text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices dropped on news that Saudi Arabia has restored crude export flows through the Red Sea to around 3.5 million barrels per day. The stock is also down 11% over the past two weeks, a period that has seen oil prices under pressure as supply concerns ease in the Middle East despite ongoing geopolitical tensions. With U.S. crude trading at $96 per barrel—a meaningful decline from earlier in September—the company faces headwinds from lower energy prices, which directly reduce revenue for oil producers.

The broader squeeze on energy stocks reflects competing forces: while Middle Eastern exports have rebounded and Canada is expanding LNG capacity (potentially adding more global supply), U.S. policymakers are considering a diesel export ban that could tighten refining margins. For an integrated company like ConocoPhillips, this mix of falling oil prices and uncertain refining conditions has weighed on investor sentiment over the past two weeks.
